text:
maria: quick QA — I applied the gateway + ALB secretbinding terraform change for the inference canary and now the canary is getting sporadic 502s. TF apply succeeded but traffic to canary endpoints shows 502s from ALB. Anyone seen this pattern?

ashok: did you move the TLS secret into a different namespace? Gateway API / ALB secret wiring is fussy — cert usually needs to be in the same namespace as the Gateway unless you use a SecretBinding controller. what did the TF change actually do? short diff pls. :eyes:

maria: diff was basically adding a gateway resource in infra namespace and a secret_binding pointing at certs/tls-inference. terraform snippet:```hcl
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "gateway" {
  manifest = file("gateway.yaml")
}
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "secretbinding" {
  manifest = file("secretbinding.yaml")
}
```
I reused the cert from certs namespace, thought SecretBinding would let us reference it.

kevin: ALB 502s often mean the target group has unhealthy targets or app returned a bad response. can you paste the ALB access log line? also check target group health — is the probe path and port correct? our service uses /live not /health by default.

maria: here's a filtered ALB log line from the canary:```2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ALB req_id=abc123 target_status=502 backend_status= - elb_status=502 "GET /api/v0/predict HTTP/1.1" host: inference.canary.app.redwood.internal````

samir: also check Host header — ALB forwards the original Host header by default. our app expects host header to be the internal FQDN (inference-api.svc.cluster.local) for virtual-host routing. if the app rejects the Host it might 502/400. with Gateway API you can add a RequestHeaderModifier filter to rewrite Host. example:```yaml
filters:
- type: RequestHeaderModifier
  requestHeaderModifier:
    set:
    - name: Host
      value: inference-api.svc.cluster.local
```
This has saved me before when frontend uses the public host.

ashok: +1 on Host header. Also double-check that the TLS secret is accessible to the Gateway. If you used the cert from another namespace without a proper SecretBinding controller, the Gateway will present no cert and ALB may fall back and then mismatch SNI causing handshake errors upstream. But your ALB log shows 502 from backend, so TLS likely OK at LB.

kevin: run these quick checks:```bash
kubectl get gateway -n infra -o yaml
kubectl get secret tls-inference -n certs -o yaml
kubectl get httproute -n infra -o yaml
kubectl describe tg <alb-target-group-id> # (aws cli)
```
and `kubectl get endpoints -n inference` — make sure endpoints are actually healthy and port matches service.targetPort.

maria: endpoints look odd — service port is named `http` and targetPort is 8081, but container is listening on 8080. svc:```ports:
- name: http
  port: 80
  targetPort: 8081
```
endpoints show pod IPs on 8080. maybe that explains the 502.

samir: yep that will cause connection refused from target and ALB returns 502. two fixes: update service.targetPort to 8080, or change containerPort/startup to 8081. if you're patching quick: `kubectl patch svc inference-api -n inference --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":8080}]'`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Terraform apply completed for module/gateway infra gateway.tf (plan_id=plan-2026-03-15-14) :white_check_mark:

kevin: also after you fix port mismatch, update the HTTPRoute to include the RequestHeaderModifier filter from samir if the app still fails due to Host. and ensure LGTM for secret placement — if Gateway can't access the cert, kubernetes events on the Gateway will indicate TLS errors. `kubectl describe gateway -n infra` will show it.

maria: thanks — I'll patch the svc targetPort first and move a copy of the TLS secret into the infra namespace (quick workaround) and add the header modifier. will report back in ~20m. :thumbsup:
